comments.comment: I am  thankful my insomnia led me to this interview from midnight to 2:48 am. Only now discovering Mr. Greene through this interview having read none of his books I have now become a fan of you both for different reasons. I identify with Mr. Greene interests in human nature and behavior, and the challenges he currently faces .  I have played the role of caregiver thrice in my short 65 years on earth. The first was a conscious choice to help my mother die with dignity in her home after a terminal cancer diagnosis(1998). The second was an ageing neighbor and friend estranged from family by distance and prison parole restrictions who suffered a stroke at least twice as well as fractured limbs  eventually succumbing to Covid-19 in a state nursing home(2021). The third is a former lover I met in 1979 until 1987 when he left me because my crack addiction during the HIV epidemic. Our orbits intersected once again 20 years later. He was disabled by a fall on ice requiring double shoulder surgery and I was living in a bedbug infested single room but employed during the banking collapse at the end of Bush Jr. presidency. He had another accidental fall requiring doible knee surgery followed by a successful remission of prostate cancer. So yeah life is what it is but there's never a dull moment. Always grateful  for a new day. I enjoy your interview style that lets viewers feel like their sitting right there at your table. KUDOS!

comments.comment: The thing about bringing women to cheap or expensive places is this: 53:20  Choosing a place is very much like choosing a song to play in your car because you are essentially telling a story about yourself. If you only listen to Disney music, well, that says something about you. Or if you only listen to Bethoven then that also says something about you.   We're constantly comparing our stories to see if we share anything in common because that will ultimately make or break the relationship. I once dated someone who came from a wealthy family and he offered to bring me to fancy places except I was never comfortable because I came from a poor family. Instead, I often chose to eat at cheap places because therein lies my emotional attachment and I wished for him to partake in my story. We stopped going out after a few dates because it became apparent that we were too different even though he was a lovely man.   (oh and by the way, I'm fairly rich myself and can take care of myself independently hence I wasn't looking for a man with money. I was just looking for good company.)  The MOST SEDUCTIVE thing is finding someone who is able understand and expand your story, but also does it effortlessly. If you are cheap, find a man who is happy to be cheap with you. And if you desire luxury, then find a man who doesn't mind pampering you. The only caveat is that we don't overdo it and that we mix it up once in a while for the sake of adventure and excitement.   I wouldn't mind if a man brought me to a cheap place as long his idea of cheapness is similar to mine. I don't want to eat next to the sewer in a cardboard box because I wasn't brought up that way, but a roadside stall with good food? Yeah, sign me up!
